extraction.name: RoboFAC dataset
extraction.description: A dataset for robotic failure analysis and correction comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 1,282 successful trajectories (totaling 10,722 trajectories) and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation (ManiSkill) and real-world environments. The dataset categorizes failures across three hierarchical levels (Task Planning, Motion Planning, Execution Control) and provides multi-dimensional question-answer annotations for eight distinct question types.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao
extraction.citeAs: Lu, W., Ye, M., Ye, Z., Tao, R., Yang, S., & Zhao, B. (2025). RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction. arXiv preprint arXiv:2505.12224v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collection occurred in both simulated and real-world environments. In simulation, 14 robotic tasks were implemented in ManiSkill with objects from YCB and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Expert policies were defined by specifying target end-effector poses, and erroneous trajectories were created by perturbing or replacing policy code snippets at selected substages. In the real world, data for 6 tasks were collected via teleoperation using an SO-100 robotic arm across 3 synchronized viewpoints.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments, Physical data collection, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Simulated trajectories recorded in the ManiSkill robotics simulation environment with YCB objects, ReplicaCAD, and AI2-THOR scenes; real-world robotic execution videos recorded using an SO-100 robotic arm.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Because motion planning occasionally failed and led to trajectories inconsistent with textual descriptions, manual data cleaning was performed, retaining approximately 75% of the collected simulation data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: QA samples covering eight question types were generated using five distinct phrasing templates per type. For deterministic questions (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, failure locating), reference answers were directly extracted from recorded textual descriptions. For failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction, prompts and videos paired with description files were fed into GPT-4o to generate answers, followed by manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current integration of the correction model into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless, and the model was exclusively applied to a single VLA model rather than hierarchical policies.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Robotic failure detection, task understanding, failure analysis, failure correction, fine-tuning multimodal large language models (MLLMs), and evaluating robotic failure video comprehension.
